configKeys.effect: Config comment: "Range in blocks to detect players and become hostile". Radius of the axis-aligned box (getBoundingBox().inflate(range), HostileZombifiedPiglinsModule.java:164-166) in which the module looks for a player to pin the piglin's grudge on, and outside of which it wipes that grudge again. It is NOT attack range: the actual chase is vanilla's NearestAttackableTargetGoal, capped at the FOLLOW_RANGE attribute (35 blocks for a zombified piglin) and requiring line of sight, so values above ~35 only extend the zone in which a grudge is kept alive, not the distance from which piglins come at you. Creative and spectator players are never detected.

Config comment: "How long zombified piglins stay angry in ticks (-1 for indefinite)". Effectively a two-state switch, NOT a duration. Any value >= 0 is written at HostileZombifiedPiglinsModule.java:146 and then immediately overwritten at L149 by startPersistentAngerTimer(), which in vanilla 1.21.1 rolls a fresh random 400-780 ticks (ZombifiedPiglin.java:176-177) - so 200 behaves exactly like 5 or like 2000000000. Only -1 is observably different, and it works through a separate path: maintainHostility re-sets the timer to Integer.MAX_VALUE once per second while a player is in range (L244-248). In all cases the anger is zeroed the moment no eligible player is inside detection_range.

Config comment: "Time in seconds before a zombified piglin can switch to a new nearest player target". Wall-clock seconds (`System.currentTimeMillis()`, converted to ms by `getTargetSwitchThresholdValue(true)`), so it is unaffected by TPS, lag or a paused single-player world. It does NOT measure how long the grudge has been held: the holder's timestamp is refreshed on every once-per-second pass in which it is still first in the query (HostileZombifiedPiglinsModule.java:213-218), so the clock only starts running once somebody else takes the front of the list. An old grudge is therefore no easier to displace than a fresh one. The "nearest" player is simply the first the level query returns - the list is never sorted - and on an actual switch the timestamp is not carried over fresh (:200-212), so the new holder settles only on the following pass.

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.EntityJoinLevelEvent (game bus; fires on BOTH sides - the client path stores a null map entry and is otherwise inert)

net.neoforged.neoforge.event.tick.EntityTickEvent.Pre (game bus, fires on both sides for every ticking entity; the body returns immediately on the client and is throttled to every 20th tick per entity)
notes:
SOURCE FOOTPRINT: three files, 381 lines total. modules/hostile_zombified_piglins/HostileZombifiedPiglinsModule.java (250 lines), .../config/HostileZombifiedPiglinsConfig.java (121), .../models/NearestPlayerTime.java (11), plus the standalone entrypoint standalone/hostile_zombified_piglins/HostileZombifiedPiglinsStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_hostile_zombified_piglins"), boots via StandaloneModuleBootstrap). NO mixins (no mixin/hostile_zombified_piglins/ directory; grep for "piglin" in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json returns nothing), NO DeferredRegister of any kind (grep for DeferredRegister/DeferredHolder/KeyMapping/Payload/@JeiPlugin in the module directory: none), NO assets and NO data files (find over src/main/resources for *piglin*/*zombified*: nothing), NO lang keys (en_us.json has no piglin/zombified entry - the module produces no player-visible text at all, only logger output). build.gradle:441 registers the standalone jar as a bare one-liner with no mixins:, clientMixins:, dataGlobs: or moduleDeps:. Bundle registration is unconditional at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:153. No docs/modules/hostile_zombified_piglins.md exists yet - README.md:42-43 is currently the only documentation.

### THE BIG ONE - anger_duration IS DEAD CONFIG (never reaches the entity)
makeHostileToPlayer sets the timer from the config (L141-147: angerDuration, or Integer.MAX_VALUE when -1) and then, two lines later, calls zombifiedPiglin.startPersistentAngerTimer() (L149). In vanilla 1.21.1 that method is NOT a "start the timer I just set" call - ZombifiedPiglin.java:176-177 is `this.setRemainingPersistentAngerTime(PERSISTENT_ANGER_TIME.sample(this.random))` with PERSISTENT_ANGER_TIME = TimeUtil.rangeOfSeconds(20, 39) (ZombifiedPiglin.java:52). So the configured value is OVERWRITTEN one line later by a random 400-780 ticks, every single time. Consequences:
  * Any anger_duration >= 0 produces exactly the same in-game behaviour: 20-39 seconds of vanilla-rolled anger. Setting it to 1 or to 2000000000 changes nothing observable.
  * anger_duration = -1 ("indefinite") still works, but NOT through makeHostileToPlayer - it works because maintainHostility's tail (L244-248) re-sets the timer to Integer.MAX_VALUE once per second whenever the configured value is -1 and the remaining time has fallen below Integer.MAX_VALUE/2.
  * A doc page must NOT describe anger_duration as "how many ticks they chase you". The honest description is: "-1 = never calms down while you are in range; any other value = vanilla's own 20-39 s anger, refreshed for as long as you stay in range." (This corrects the earlier survey, which assumed the configured value was applied and merely topped up.)

ANGER DOES NOT DECAY WHILE THE PIGLIN HAS YOU AS ITS TARGET. Vanilla NeutralMob.updatePersistentAnger(level, true) (NeutralMob.java:58-76) only decrements the timer when the current target is null or is not a Player (L69). ZombifiedPiglin.customServerAiStep calls it with updateAnger = true (ZombifiedPiglin.java:109). So once the piglin has actually acquired the player, the anger clock is frozen; it only runs down in the gaps where it has no active target. Together with the module's once-per-second top-up at L222-224 (`!isAngryAt(newTarget) || getRemainingPersistentAngerTime() < 100`), a piglin that can see you never calms down on its own.

detection_range IS NOT ATTACK RANGE. getNearbyPlayers (L154-168) uses level.getEntitiesOfClass(Player.class, getBoundingBox().inflate(detectionRange), ...), i.e. an axis-aligned CUBE: detection_range = 32 is a ~65-block cube, not a 32-block sphere. But flagging a player as the persistent anger target is all this module does - it never calls setTarget(). The actual hunting is vanilla's NearestAttackableTargetGoal<>(this, Player.class, 10, true, false, this::isAngryAt) (ZombifiedPiglin.java:75), whose TargetingConditions are forCombat().range(getFollowDistance()) (NearestAttackableTargetGoal.java:44). FOLLOW_RANGE for a zombified piglin is the inherited Zombie value of 35.0 (Zombie.java:122; ZombifiedPiglin.createAttributes does not override it), forCombat() has checkLineOfSight = true (TargetingConditions.java:14+23), and mustSee = true. So: the piglin cannot start chasing you beyond ~35 blocks or through solid blocks no matter how high detection_range is set, and raising detection_range past ~35 only widens the radius in which the module *pre-assigns* you as its grudge - which still matters, because it also decides when the anger is CLEARED (see below). Creative and spectator players are excluded from detection (L166 predicate).

IT IS NOT "THE NEAREST PLAYER" - CONTRADICTS THE README. getNearbyPlayers returns the raw level query result; the callers take nearbyPlayers.getFirst() (L133, L184) and the list is never sorted by distance. The variable is called nearestPlayer and the config key is target_switch_threshold, but the chosen grudge-holder is simply whichever player the entity-section query happened to return first. The README's "smart targeting and player switching" (README.md:43) overstates this. (Vanilla's own goal does pick the genuinely nearest eligible player via Level.getNearestPlayer - but only among players the module has already flagged, so in a multiplayer Nether the module can hand the piglin a grudge against a far-away player while a closer one walks past unmolested.)

NOT LIMITED TO THE NETHER. There is no dimension check anywhere in the module (unlike hostile_endermen, which gates on the End). Every ZombifiedPiglin in every dimension is affected - Overworld piglins created by a pig struck by lightning, piglins that zombified after wandering through a portal, piglins in the End. The README's "in the Nether" describes where they normally live, not a code gate.

WALK AWAY AND THEY FORGET YOU INSTANTLY. The javadoc claim "Removes the 'forgiveness' mechanic where they calm down over time" (L27) is only half true. While you are in range they never calm down, but the moment a maintainHostility tick finds no eligible player in the detection cube it does setRemainingPersistentAngerTime(0) + setPersistentAngerTarget(null) and drops the map entry (L185-195, and again at L232-239). That is a HARSHER reset than vanilla, which would keep the grudge for 20-39 s. Switching to creative or spectator also counts as leaving (the L166 predicate), and so does going more than detection_range away on any axis.

PACK BEHAVIOUR IS NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE. The javadoc bullet "Maintains pack behavior where attacking one angers nearby ones" (L28) describes vanilla ZombifiedPiglin.maybeAlertOthers/alertOthers (ZombifiedPiglin.java:131-151, FOLLOW_RANGE-wide, requires line of sight to the current target, only recruits piglins whose getTarget() is null). The module neither adds nor touches it. It does interact with it, though: because the module keeps piglins angry, they have targets more often, so alertOthers fires more often.

SINGLE-PLAYER: THE MAP IS SHARED BETWEEN THE CLIENT AND THE INTEGRATED SERVER, UNSYNCHRONISED. angryPiglins is a plain java.util.HashMap field on the single module instance (L41). onEntityJoinLevel (L71-85) is NOT side-gated - EntityJoinLevelEvent is posted from ClientLevel.addEntity too (ClientLevel.java:352, verified in the decompiled 1.21.1+NeoForge sources), and the entity UUID is the same on both sides. In an integrated server (single player / LAN) that means:
  * The client render thread and the server thread both mutate the same HashMap with no synchronisation. This is a genuine data race; a concurrent put during a resize can corrupt the table.
  * The client's join handler stores null for a UUID the server had just filled in (makeHostileToPlayer -> getNearbyPlayers returns null on the client at L155, so the whole call returns null and HashMap happily stores the null value). The server's target/timestamp bookkeeping for that piglin is therefore wiped at spawn, so target_switch_threshold effectively restarts. maintainHostility bails client-side at L174, so client-written entries are never cleaned up by the client.
On a dedicated server neither problem exists (no client in the JVM).

MEMORY: ENTRIES ARE ONLY EVER REMOVED WHEN NO PLAYER IS IN RANGE. angryPiglins.remove() appears exactly twice (L187, L233), both on the "nobody nearby" path. A piglin that dies, despawns, is killed by the player or unloads while a player is still in range leaves its entry behind forever - there is no death/unload/level-unload handler. NearestPlayerTime holds a strong Player reference, so a stale entry pins a ServerPlayer (and through it the level) after logout. The map is a transient in-memory field, never persisted and never cleared on server stop; it is rebuilt from scratch after a restart. The piglins' vanilla persistent anger (AngerTime/AngryAt NBT) IS saved by vanilla, independently of this module. Note also that null values occur on the SERVER too: a piglin that spawns with no player in range stores a null entry at L79 (L126-131 returns null), which is cleaned up by the next maintainHostility pass.

TARGET-SWITCH BOOKKEEPING IS WALL-CLOCK AND SLIGHTLY BROKEN. The threshold is compared against System.currentTimeMillis() (L151, L200, L206-207), so it is real time - unaffected by server lag, TPS, or a paused single-player world. And when the target actually switches (L208) the new entry keeps the PREVIOUS target's timestamp, because newTimeStamp is only refreshed in the non-switch branch (L200-201 vs. L217). The freshly switched target therefore starts out already past its threshold; it self-corrects one second later via the else-if at L214-218, as long as the same player stays first in the query result.

STALE INLINE COMMENT: L207 reads `> getConfig().getTargetSwitchThresholdValue(true)) { // 10 seconds threshold`, but the configured default is 5.0 seconds (HostileZombifiedPiglinsConfig.java:71). The comment is wrong; the code is right.

THROTTLE IS PER-ENTITY, NOT GLOBAL. onEntityTick (L91-105) gates on event.getEntity().tickCount % 20 != 0, so each piglin is processed once per second - but the handler itself still runs for every ticking entity in the game, on both sides, before the instanceof check. The isModuleEnabled() check (L92-94) is the first thing in the method, so a disabled module costs only that call.

ENABLE GATE DIFFERS BETWEEN BUNDLE AND STANDALONE JAR (same pattern as the other modules). onInitialize (L52-58) subscribes to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS unconditionally; isModuleEnabled() is only consulted inside the two handlers.
  * BUNDLE: ModuleManager.initializeModules (ModuleManager.java:53-114) builds enabledModules from ModulesConfig.isModuleEnabled(module) first and calls initialize() only for those. A module switched off in the config at startup never subscribes, so a runtime enable cannot bring it back; a runtime disable does work.
  * STANDALONE JAR: StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot calls module.initialize() unconditionally (shouldInitialize() is not overridden), so both directions work at runtime.

DEAD CODE:
  * L230: commented-out `// angryPiglins.put(zombifiedPiglin.getUUID(), targetPlayerTime);`
  * HostileZombifiedPiglinsConfig.getDetectionRange() / getAngerDuration() / getTargetSwitchThreshold() (the raw ModConfigSpec accessors, L37/L46/L55) - grep over src/main/java finds no caller for any of the three.
  * HostileZombifiedPiglinsConfig.getTargetSwitchThresholdValue() (the no-arg overload, L118-120) - never called; only the (boolean) overload at L113 is used, always with true.
  * NearestPlayerTime implements Comparable and defines compareTo (models/NearestPlayerTime.java:6-10), but nothing ever sorts or compares NearestPlayerTime.
  * L34-40 is a stream-of-consciousness design comment ("2 mins later: ..."), design rationale rather than documentation.
No TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers exist anywhere in the module directory.

CONFIG: buildModuleSpecificConfig (HostileZombifiedPiglinsConfig.java:59-74) defines exactly the three keys listed above; `enabled` and `debug_logging` come from AbstractModuleConfig and are excluded from configKeys by convention. isEnabledByDefault() is not overridden anywhere in the module, so the Module interface default `true` applies (Module.java:73-75). All three *Value() getters fall back to the literal default when the spec is not built yet (L95/L104/L114) - note the target_switch_threshold fallback is written as `5` (int literal widened to 5.0), which matches the declared 5.0 default.

oneLiner: Zombified piglins come after you unprovoked - the module pins a grudge on them the moment they spawn and keeps renewing it for as long as you stay inside the detection range, so you never get the vanilla grace period; step far enough away and they forget you instantly.
shortDescription: Makes zombified piglins always aggressive towards players, creating a more challenging Nether experience
